name: s3:GetObject on a concrete-bucket object ARN (arn:aws:s3:::my-bucket/prefix/*) is NOT broad exfil
note: S1-dataexfil-arn over-correction guard. Closing the ARN-wildcard DATA-EXFIL fail-open must NOT start flagging genuinely-scoped ARNs as account-wide. Here the bucket-name head is a CONCRETE name (my-bucket) and only the trailing key is wildcarded (prefix/*), so the read is confined to one bucket's prefix - routine least privilege. DATA-EXFIL requires a BROAD resource (bare '*', NotResource, or an ARN whose partition/service/bucket-head is a leading wildcard); this is none of those.
rationale: An S3 object ARN whose bucket segment is a concrete name (my-bucket) scopes the grant to exactly that bucket; the trailing 'prefix/*' wildcard narrows to a key prefix WITHIN that bucket - it does not widen the bucket set. This is the textbook least-privilege object-read shape and matches all/nearly-all ARNs of nothing beyond one bucket, so no broad-scope bulk-read (DATA-EXFIL) or wildcard-resource (WILDCARD-RESOURCE) capability exists. The bucket name (my-bucket) carries no sensitivity token and the ARN holds no policy variable, so DATA-READ (inferred-sensitivity / variable-scoped) also stays quiet. Broadness is a property of a LEADING wildcard on a high-order ARN segment (partition/service) or on the resource-id head (the bucket name), not of a trailing key wildcard. Ref: AWS S3 ARN format arn:aws:s3:::bucket_name/key_name and IAM least-privilege guidance.
